CUSTOM_SONOFF_SNZB-06P24.description: CUSTOM PROFILE SONOFF SNZB-06P24 Presence Sensor with Zone Detection

attributes.name: fadingTime
attributes.title: Fading Time
attributes.description: Time before changing to unoccupied (Occupied to Unoccupied Delay). 30 s or more is recommended to reduce missed detections.

attributes.name: zoneStatus
attributes.description: Which detection zone is currently occupied, same bit layout as zoneEnable. Reported about once per second while someone is present.

attributes.name: zoneEnable
attributes.title: Detection Zones Bitmap
attributes.description: Enable/disable the detection zones. Zone1(0-1m)=bits 0+1, Zone2(1-1.5m)=bit 2, Zone3(1.5-2m)=bit 3, Zone4(2-2.5m)=bit 4, Zone5(2.5-3m)=bit 5, Zone6(3-3.5m)=bit 6, Zone7(3.5-4m)=bit 7. 255 = all zones enabled. Tip: use the setZone / setAllZones commands instead of calculating the bitmap by hand.

attributes.name: radarSensitivity
attributes.title: Fine-tune Sensitivity
attributes.description: Radar sensitivity fine adjustment. Negative values make the sensor less sensitive, positive values more sensitive.

comments: CUSTOM SONOFF SNZB-06P24 Zigbee Presence Sensor with 7-Zone Detection and Illuminance
Zone mapping: bit 0+1=Zone1(0-1m), bit 2=Zone2(1-1.5m), bit 3=Zone3(1.5-2m), bit 4=Zone4(2-2.5m), bit 5=Zone5(2.5-3m), bit 6=Zone6(3-3.5m), bit 7=Zone7(3.5-4m)
Zone Enable bitmap: Set bits to enable zones. Zone 1 requires both bits 0 and 1. E.g., 255 (0xFF) = all zones enabled
Calibration: use the 'spatialLearning' command (cluster 0xFC11 cluster-specific command 0x04, payload = subCmd 0x00 + uint64 LE timestamp in ms). Keep the room EMPTY while the countdown is running!
Manufacturer code 0x1286 (Shenzhen Coolkit) is required for the 0xFC11 attributes and for the spatial learning command

Attribute 0x2015 (zoneStatus) is implemented in neither Zigbee2MQTT nor ZHA, but it is real - verified on device 2026-08-24. The device pushes 0x2016 and 0x2015 together about once per second while a person is present, so this is a chatty attribute. Read responses use encoding 0x19 (BITMAP16), unsolicited reports use 0x21 (UINT16); only 0x19 matters, because it is used for writes.

Attribute 0x2021 (radarSensitivity / Fine-tune Sensitivity, INT8, -6..6) is declared by Zigbee2MQTT and by the ZHA quirk. On 2026-08-24 the test device answered a READ of it with status 0x86 UNSUPPORTED_ATTRIBUTE, while 0x2015, 0x2016, 0x2017 and 0x2018 all answered normally with the same manufacturer-specific frame - so that read failure is genuine and most likely means older firmware. It is kept in the profile anyway: a WRITE is a separate operation and is untested, and this is the only sensitivity control the device exposes. Watch for a Write Attributes Response with status 0x00 to confirm the write is accepted.

Attribute 0x2017 exists but is NOT the enum8 'learning state' the ZHA quirk assumes: this firmware returns a ZCL ARRAY (encoding 0x48) of 16 uint8 - verified on device 2026-08-24. It is deliberately NOT in this profile, since the deviceProfile attribute processing can only handle numeric values. The spatialLearningState attribute is driven by the cluster-specific 0x04 command responses instead.
ZHA quirk (still an open pull request): https://github.com/zigpy/zha-device-handlers/pull/4907 (zhaquirks/sonoff/snzb06p24.py)
